back: The line of greatest depth and fastest flow along a channel; it swings to the outside of each meander bend.
Hydraulic action, abrasion (corrasion), attrition, solution (corrosion) and cavitation.
Traction (boulders roll), saltation (sand hops), suspension (silt and clay) and solution (dissolved minerals).
A corkscrew flow in a bend: surface water moves to the outer bank and returns along the bed to the inner bank, carrying sediment to the inside.
Cross-sectional area ÷ wetted perimeter; the larger it is, the more efficient the channel.
Channel length ÷ straight-line distance; about 1.5 or more is meandering.

front: Formation of a waterfall and gorge
back: Hard rock over soft rock: the soft rock is undercut, the hard rock collapses, the fall retreats upstream and leaves a gorge.
Upper: V-valleys, rapids, waterfalls, gorges. Middle: meanders, river cliffs, point bars. Lower: floodplain, levees, oxbow lakes, deltas.
